plan: Finalized design delivered with four inline closure-notes (U10–U13): (U10) group_size=128 applied uniformly to all 7 linear projections per transformer block (q/k/v/o + gate/up/down); embedding and LM head stay fp16 — locked in §2.2. (U11) collapse_rate, degradation_slope, non_monotonicity, and H1 are defined via mean-over-6-tasks zero-shot accuracy; per-task accuracy reported in an Appendix table as diagnostic only and excluded from hypothesis testing and collapse criteria — locked in §2.3 and §5. (U12) ARC-Challenge and BoolQ contribute only accuracy signal via lm-eval-harness; PPL is computed exclusively on WT2/PTB/C4 — locked in §5 as a one-line clarification. (U13) RTN@W4 retained as critical anchor for degradation_slope_total and slope_segment 4→3; final evaluation matrix = 4 methods × 3 bits × 2 models = 24 quantized cells + 2 FP references = 26 main cells, RTN@W4 present for both 7B and 13B. Final summary block states "Open uncertainties: none" with all U1–U13 traced to closure, Assumptions A1–A16 retained as policy plus new A17 codifying the closures. Runtime untouched; all compute figures remain paper estimates on a single A100 80GB.

context.question: How does the inclusion of QuaRot's Hadamard transformation improve the quality of weight-only quantized models under low-precision settings? Can QuaRot stabilize and improve performance at 2–4 bit weight precision where traditional quantization methods like RTN and GPTQ often fail?
context.context: Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run.
